nodes.milcz.options.[dobra].text.t: Maybe you've heard of me from the front.

nodes.milcz.options.[nikt].text.t: Someone the imperials are looking for.

nodes.milcz.options.[zla].text.t: People say all sorts of things about me.

nodes.milcz.text.t: "Everyone's new here." The guard pockets the coin and leaves, and passing the boy by the wall he winks at him. The boy walks over and adjusts his cap. "That's my brother-in-law. He stands here for anyone who comes to see me, because we've had three provocateurs this month, and two of them are floating in the port now. You didn't sell me out, didn't lie, didn't risk anything. Those live longest. So who are you?"

nodes.odmowa.options.[dobra].text.t: Maybe you've heard of me from the front.

nodes.odmowa.options.[nikt].text.t: Someone the imperials are looking for.

nodes.odmowa.options.[zla].text.t: People say all sorts of things about me.

nodes.odmowa.text.t: The guard sizes you up from boots to cap, then snorts with laughter and leaves. Passing the boy by the wall, he winks at him. The boy walks over and adjusts his cap. "That's my brother-in-law. He stands here for anyone who comes to see me, because we've had three provocateurs this month. A provocateur would've nodded and gone looking along with him. You told him to get lost. That's either courage or stupidity, and both come in handy here. Who are you?"

nodes.rep_dobra.text.t: Nipper looks you straight in the eye for the first time. "Right. The carters say there was one who didn't leave his men in the field and didn't take the money though he could've, and the imperials have a description of him. A poor one, but the boots match. Anyone can tell that tale, except you were in it a moment ago."

nodes.rep_nic.text.t: "The imperials are looking for half the town. The other half they don't need to, it comes by itself." Nipper scratches under his cap. "I've heard nothing about you, which may be a good thing. For now I'm trusting my brother-in-law. He's rarely wrong, though he buys fish terribly."

nodes.rep_zla.text.t: "I heard. I know what you did at the front, half the street does. You didn't sell out my brother-in-law today, so either you've changed or you're waiting for a better price. Either way you can live with it, as long as you know which."

nodes.s.options.[milcz].text.t: Don't know him. I'm new here.

nodes.s.options.[odmowa].text.t: Look for yourself. Not my job.

nodes.s.options.[zmyl].text.t: Saw him. Went toward the port.

nodes.s.text.t: Before you reach the wall, a town guard steps into your path, cudgel under his arm, coin between his fingers. "Halt. New here? I'm looking for a brat in a green cap. Goes by Nipper, deals in what's not allowed, and hangs around here somewhere. Ten groats in silver for whoever says where he is. Seen him?" A little behind him, by the wall, a boy in a green cap stands examining his fingernails.

nodes.wydaj.text.t: The guard shoves ten groats at you and goes to the wall. He doesn't arrest anyone. He stands next to the boy in the cap and they start talking about fish. After a moment the boy looks at you over his shoulder. "That's my brother-in-law. He stands here for anyone who comes to see me. Keep the silver, you won't sell anything dearer on this street. For small change I'll tell you what everybody knows. Nothing more."

nodes.wydaj_interes.text.t: The guard shoves ten groats at you and goes to the wall. He doesn't arrest anyone. He stands next to the boy in the cap and they both laugh. The boy walks over, not surprised at all. "That's my brother-in-law. I knew you'd do it, half the street knows what you did at the front. A provocateur wouldn't have taken it, he'd want to come out looking decent. You sell everyone, but at least we know for how much. A man like that you can do business with."

nodes.zmyl.options.[dobra].text.t: Maybe you've heard of me from the front.

nodes.zmyl.options.[nikt].text.t: Someone the imperials are looking for.

nodes.zmyl.options.[zla].text.t: People say all sorts of things about me.

nodes.zmyl.text.t: "To the port, you say." The guard looks at you a moment longer than needed, pockets the coin and leaves. Not to the port. Passing the boy by the wall, he winks at him. The boy walks over and adjusts his cap. "That's my brother-in-law. He stands here for anyone who comes to see me, because we've had three provocateurs this month, and two of them are floating in the port now. You lied to the guard for a boy you don't know and didn't take the silver. Fine. So who are you?"
